title.rendered: Your voices matter in credible elections, Obi tells diaspora Africans

content.rendered:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has called on Africans in the diaspora to actively promote good governance and advocate for free, fair and credible elections across the continent, saying their voices remain crucial in strengthening democracy.

Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Sunday, following a keynote address he delivered on Friday at the Mandela Hall of the African Union Permanent Observer Mission to the United Nations in New York.

The address was titled, “The Role of the Diaspora African in Sustainable Development across Africa.”

According to Obi, Africa possesses enormous human and natural resources but continues to grapple with widespread poverty because of poor leadership.

“Africa is a continent of immense riches. Indeed, it is the richest continent in the world, not only because of its vast mineral resources but also because of its greatest asset, its people,” he said.

He noted that the continent has more than 1.5 billion people, with over one billion young people of productive age, as well as nearly one billion hectares of arable land, about 60 per cent of which remains uncultivated.

Despite these advantages, Obi said Africa remains home to the largest concentration of people living in extreme poverty.

“The question, therefore, is simple. With all these advantages, why has Africa not been able to lift its people out of poverty?

“It means there is a missing link. That missing link is competent leadership with capacity, compassion, character and commitment to good governance,” he said.

Obi urged Africans living abroad to leverage their exposure to societies with stronger institutions and greater accountability to advocate for better governance on the continent.

“Because you live in societies where institutions largely work, where democracy is strengthened by accountability and where systems function more effectively, you have both an opportunity and a responsibility to help build Africa.

“It is time to become stronger advocates for good governance. Even where you cannot vote, your voices matter. They should be heard both at home and abroad whenever things are going wrong on our continent.

“Stand firmly for what is right. Speak truth to the leaders who visit you. Let them know where they are getting it wrong,” he said.

Obi also cited Japan, China and India as examples of countries that benefited significantly from the contributions of their diaspora communities to national development.

He said Africa’s diaspora professionals, particularly in healthcare, education and technology, could help drive similar transformation if governments created an enabling environment for them to contribute.

The former Anambra State governor further called on diaspora Africans to remain engaged in shaping the continent’s democratic future.

“Their voices matter in advancing free, fair and credible elections across Africa. Elections conducted with integrity are the foundation of legitimate governance. They create the pathway to competent leadership capable of delivering the policies, institutions and opportunities our people deserve,” he said.
